description: Entirely synthetic technical notes. Ground truth is human-declared, not inferred by the embedding vocabulary. No real user content or credentials.

notes.title: Spring WebClient response timeout
notes.summary: Bound hanging Java HTTP requests.
notes.content:
## Response deadline [eval:client-config]

Use Reactor WebClient with a response timeout. Connect timeout and response timeout cover different phases. A latency spike should not hold a request indefinitely.

```java
HttpClient client = HttpClient.create().responseTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(5));
```

- Apply the timeout before issuing HTTP work.
- Treat timeout as a failure, not a successful empty response.

notes.title: Nginx upstream read timeout
notes.summary: Reverse proxy boundaries for slow upstream responses.

notes.title: Redis caching with TTL
notes.summary: Expire cached values rather than storing them forever.
notes.content:
## Expiration [eval:redis-ttl]

Redis caching needs a TTL that reflects acceptable staleness. Cache invalidation is separate from expiration.

```text
SET article:demo synthetic-value EX 300
```

Do not treat a missing cache entry as a missing database record. A cache miss loads the source and repopulates Redis.

notes.title: Chống cache stampede với Redis
notes.summary: Khóa ngắn và jitter khi nhiều request cùng làm mới bộ nhớ đệm.
notes.content:
## Làm mới có kiểm soát [eval:redis-lock]

Khi Redis hết TTL, nhiều request có thể cùng đọc nguồn. Dùng lock ngắn để một request làm mới cache; request khác dùng giá trị cũ hoặc chờ có giới hạn. Jitter làm thời điểm hết hạn khác nhau.

```text
SET refresh:demo synthetic-owner NX PX 2000
```

Không xóa lock của request khác. Kiểm tra giá trị trước khi giải phóng khóa.

notes.title: PostgreSQL B-tree indexing
notes.summary: Use EXPLAIN before adding an index.
notes.content:
## Ordered lookup [eval:btree-plan]

A PostgreSQL B-tree index supports equality and ordered ranges. Inspect EXPLAIN to see whether the planner scans too many rows.

```sql
CREATE INDEX demo_updated ON demo_note(updated_at);
EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM demo_note ORDER BY updated_at DESC LIMIT 20;
```

An index has write and storage costs; measure the workload.

notes.title: PostgreSQL JSONB GIN index
notes.summary: Containment queries use a different index family.
notes.content:
## Containment [eval:gin-plan]

For JSONB containment in PostgreSQL, consider a GIN index rather than assuming a B-tree fits every query.

```sql
CREATE INDEX demo_payload ON demo_event USING gin(payload);
EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM demo_event WHERE payload @> '{"kind":"demo"}';
```

The index operator class must match the query.

notes.title: Docker multi-stage build
notes.summary: Separate compilation from the runtime image.
notes.content:
## Build stages [eval:docker-build]

A Docker multi-stage build compiles in one stage and copies the application into a smaller runtime image. Do not ship the compiler merely because it was needed during build.

```dockerfile
FROM eclipse-temurin:17 AS build
WORKDIR /work
COPY . .
RUN ./gradlew bootJar
FROM eclipse-temurin:17-jre
COPY --from=build /work/build/libs/demo.jar /app.jar
```

notes.title: Docker service networking
notes.summary: Container localhost is not another service.
notes.content:
## Service names [eval:docker-network]

Inside a Docker container, localhost refers to that container. Connect to another service by its network name, not the host loopback address.

```yaml
services:
  api:
    environment:
      DB_HOST: postgres
```

Exposing a port and joining a network solve different problems.

notes.title: Kafka consumer offset commits
notes.summary: Acknowledge work after processing succeeds.
notes.content:
## Commit boundary [eval:kafka-commit]

Kafka consumers should commit offsets after durable processing. A crash between processing and commit can replay records, so use idempotent effects.

```java
consumer.poll(Duration.ofMillis(500));
consumer.commitSync();
```

The example omits business processing; do not commit before that work succeeds.

notes.title: Kafka consumer rebalance
notes.summary: Keep polling responsive while handling expensive records.
notes.content:
## Poll cadence [eval:kafka-poll]

A Kafka consumer that spends too long processing may exceed max.poll.interval.ms and cause a rebalance. Bound work per poll or move processing behind a controlled handoff.

```properties
max.poll.records=100
max.poll.interval.ms=300000
```

Increasing a limit hides neither slow work nor duplicate processing.

notes.title: OAuth and OIDC login
notes.summary: Verify identity rather than trusting client-supplied ownership.
notes.content:
## Verified principal [eval:oidc-principal]

OAuth authorization and OIDC authentication are related but different. Verify issuer, audience and the signed identity claims. A server session associates the authenticated principal with application ownership.

- Do not accept owner IDs from request bodies.
- Require the expected verified email when using a single-owner allowlist.
- Keep credentials on the server.

notes.title: CSRF protection and session cookies
notes.summary: HttpOnly alone does not prevent request forgery.
notes.content:
## Mutation boundary [eval:csrf-token]

A browser attaches session cookies automatically. CSRF defenses protect state-changing HTTP requests against forgery. HttpOnly reduces script access to the cookie but is not a CSRF token.

```text
POST /api/demo
X-CSRF-TOKEN: synthetic-placeholder
```

Validate origin and forward the session's token on the server; never put session credentials in an article.

notes.title: Kubernetes readiness and liveness
notes.summary: Serving eligibility differs from process recovery.
notes.content:
## Probe roles [eval:probe-roles]

Kubernetes readiness determines whether a pod receives traffic. Liveness determines whether a process should restart. A temporary dependency failure must not necessarily restart every pod.

```yaml
readinessProbe:
  httpGet: {path: /ready, port: 8080}
livenessProbe:
  httpGet: {path: /live, port: 8080}
```

notes.title: Kubernetes rolling updates
notes.summary: Use readiness before admitting a replacement pod.
notes.content:
## Deployment transition [eval:rollout-ready]

Kubernetes rolling updates replace pods gradually. Readiness keeps an initializing pod outside the serving set. A rollout budget balances temporary extra pods against unavailable capacity.

```yaml
strategy:
  rollingUpdate: {maxSurge: 1, maxUnavailable: 0}
```

Readiness is a prerequisite, not a complete availability guarantee.

notes.title: Jackson JSON serialization
notes.summary: Stable Java DTOs should not expose persistence entities.
notes.content:
## DTO shape [eval:jackson-dto]

Jackson JSON serialization maps explicit Java DTO fields to a wire contract. Avoid exposing an entity graph by accident.

```java
record DemoResponse(String title, String summary) {}
```

Test missing fields, unknown fields and nested records. Serialization compatibility is part of API design.

notes.title: Java serialization compatibility
notes.summary: Native object streams and JSON are not the same format.
notes.content:
## Native stream version [eval:serial-version]

Java native serialization stores object graph data. serialVersionUID controls one compatibility check but does not make untrusted streams safe.

```java
private static final long serialVersionUID = 1L;
```

Prefer an explicit data contract when crossing trust boundaries. A JSON DTO is a separate representation.

notes.title: Next.js server-side transport
notes.summary: Focused BFF calls keep backend addresses and session forwarding server-side.
notes.content:
## Focused transport [eval:next-transport]

A Next.js BFF forwards a session cookie to a backend only from server-side code. Server Actions perform explicit mutations, not domain authorization.

```typescript
fetch(backendUrl, { cache: 'no-store', headers: { Cookie: incomingCookie } });
```

Do not expose provider credentials through browser configuration.

notes.title: Next.js private read caching
notes.summary: No-store avoids serving stale private workspace reads.
notes.content:
## Dynamic reads [eval:next-cache]

Next.js private server reads should use no-store when the underlying data changes per session. This is different from a shared Redis cache.

```typescript
fetch(backendUrl, { cache: 'no-store' });
```

Dynamic rendering is not a substitute for backend authentication.

notes.title: Tệp đính kèm S3 và MinIO
notes.summary: Upload vào bucket riêng và kiểm tra quyền ở backend.
notes.content:
## Quyền truy cập [eval:minio-upload]

S3 và MinIO lưu tệp trong bucket riêng. Attachment upload cần kiểm tra media type, kích thước và quyền sở hữu. Backend trả định danh ổn định, không trả object key bí mật cho trình duyệt.

- Chỉ chấp nhận loại tệp cho phép.
- Không cấp quyền public cho toàn bucket.
- Khi xóa ghi chú, xử lý attachment bằng hàng đợi bền vững.

notes.title: S3 presigned delivery
notes.summary: A short-lived URL is a scoped capability.
notes.content:
## Expiry [eval:s3-expiry]

An S3 presigned URL permits one bucket operation until expiry. Keep the bucket private and avoid logging the full capability URL. For application attachments, access-scoped delivery must honor current visibility.

Do not copy a real signed URL into documentation. This synthetic note contains no token or credential.

notes.title: pgvector current-set retrieval
notes.summary: Cosine retrieval excludes stale and incomplete embeddings.
notes.content:
## Compatible set [eval:vector-current]

PostgreSQL pgvector cosine retrieval uses only complete embedding sets for current content and the configured model dimensions. Changed content stales the old set before replacement.

```sql
SELECT embedding <=> query_vector AS distance;
```

Nearest distance is not a percentage confidence score. Owner filtering precedes retrieval.

notes.title: GitHub Actions independent jobs
notes.summary: Keep API and Web CI validation independently visible.
notes.content:
## Regression pipeline [eval:actions-jobs]

GitHub Actions runs separate CI jobs for Java API and Next.js Web. A workflow should run tests and build, not trust a local claim of success.

```yaml
jobs:
  api:
    steps:
      - run: ./gradlew clean build
  web:
    steps:
      - run: npm test
```

This note is synthetic; evaluation does not inspect or rerun workflows.

notes.title: HTTP forward proxy configuration
notes.summary: Forwarding traffic differs from an application reverse proxy.
notes.content:
## Forward route [eval:proxy-connect]

An HTTP forward proxy mediates outbound requests. CONNECT tunnels a destination connection; forwarded headers identify the original route only when trusted hops validate them. Nginx reverse proxy configuration solves a different direction of traffic.

Do not forward credentials to an arbitrary proxy. Document the trust boundary and preserve TLS validation.
